title: Multimodal Verifier Agents for Adaptive Workflow Re-planning
research_question: Can a multi-agent workflow that inserts a dedicated multimodal verifier to check cross-modal grounding before execution reduce error propagation and unnecessary re-planning compared with standard planner-executor LLM workflows?
hypothesis: A verifier agent that explicitly tests whether plans remain grounded in both visual and textual evidence will detect latent cross-modal mismatches early, leading to fewer downstream failures and more efficient adaptive re-planning than baseline multi-agent workflows without verification.
motivation: The knowledge base highlights a recurring gap around uncertainty handling in adaptive systems: existing approaches improve adaptation decisions, but explicit model-selection uncertainty and heterogeneous requirements remain underexplored. At the same time, previously rejected ideas in agentic orchestration cluster around generic uncertainty averaging and escalation policies, suggesting that another generic risk-aware orchestration idea would be insufficiently novel. A more promising direction is to transfer adaptive-system uncertainty handling into agentic AI workflows, but do so through a concrete and testable mechanism: multimodal verification of plan grounding before execution. This targets a likely failure mode in emerging AI systems—cross-modal hallucination and mis-grounded plans—while staying distinct from rejected orchestration proposals by focusing on verifier-driven adaptive re-planning rather than uncertainty averaging alone.
